definition: Language shift is the process in which a minority or heritage language loses strength across time as people move toward greater use and proficiency in the wider societal language. In this context, it is tied to erosion or attrition of the heritage language and can contribute to breaks in language continuity between generations.

reasons: The packet supports that heritage bilingualism literature highlights “language shift and erosion” and that these relate to intergenerational discontinuity, but it does not explicitly support the framing that language shift is specifically “the process in which a minority or heritage language loses strength across time” *because* people move toward “greater use and proficiency in the wider societal language.”

The definition’s claim that language shift is “in this context” tied to “erosion or attrition of the heritage language” and that it “can contribute to breaks in language continuity between generations” is broadly consistent with the packet’s wording (“language shift and erosion,” “attrition in heritage language proficiency,” and “intergenerational language discontinuity”), but the unsupported causal/process framing in the first sentence makes the definition not fully supported by the packet.
